    <h2>About me</h2>
    <p>I grew up in Trieste, a city in the north-east of Italy, where the fresh, salty sea air carries a breath of science and innovation. There I studied physics and specialised in cosmology, the branch of physics shared by theoretical physics and astrophysics that studies our Universe's birth, history and structure at very large scales.</p>
    <p>During my PhD at <a href="https://www.sissa.it">SISSA</a>, an international school of excellence devoted entirely to doctoral research, and later as a member of the <a href="https://cosmology.unige.ch/">cosmology group</a> at the University of Geneva, I contributed to understanding why the Universe we live in is in a phase of accelerated expansion. The cause of this acceleration is a mysterious element of reality called Dark Energy, so elusive that what it is made of and how we can describe it mathematically remain unclear.</p>
    <p>My job sat at the intersection between theory and observations. With my expertise in both mathematical modelling and data analysis, I studied if and how current (and future) data themselves can lead us to a better understanding of the underlying theory that describes Dark Energy. To this end, I built and used Bayesian inference tools to test a variety of models based on general relativity, in the quest to find the one that truly describes the Universe's evolution.</p>
    <p>Along the way, I led several projects and international teams, taught at university level in English and French, and founded the <a href="https://indico-dpt.unige.ch/event/1/">CosmoFONDUE conference</a> with my colleagues at UniGe.</p>
    <p>After six years in academia, I decided to challenge myself in a new context. I am now moving into industry, eager to bring my expertise in bridging theoretical models and data to problems on far smaller scales than the cosmos. In particular, I am drawn to how data can offer powerful insights into health and help improve people's lives.</p>
    <p>With this goal in mind, I am adapting and expanding my skills for real-world, industry settings: I am earning certifications in project management and data science, deepening my knowledge of machine-learning theory and tools, and keeping pace with the fast-moving world of AI.</p>
    <p>In the meantime, I have started working on my first health-data project: exploring whether basal body temperature can offer new insights into endometriosis and support its diagnosis. Follow my progress on my <a href="projects.html">projects page</a> and on <a href="https://github.com/mberti94">GitHub</a>.</p>
    <p>My journey through physics took me from Trieste to Geneva, and I now live in Lausanne. Outside work, I love singing (I have sung soprano in a baroque choir for more than ten years and used to conduct an amateur ensemble), classical ballet and knitting.</p>
    <p>If you share an interest in data, science or health tech, or see an opportunity to work together, I would be glad to connect.</p>
    <p>Thank you for getting to know me!</p>
  </div>
